key_insight: Polygenic scores, especially for ADHD and educational attainment, showed modest associations with ADHD symptom levels and treatment-related change in a pediatric medication cohort.
clinical_relevance: This suggests genetic and clinical data together may help stratify ADHD medication response in the future, but the findings are not yet ready for routine prediction in practice.
method: Prospective Swedish ADAPT cohort of 309 children and adolescents starting ADHD medication.
Calculated polygenic scores for ADHD, autism, educational attainment, and intelligence.
Used mixed-effects models and machine learning to test links between genetics, symptoms, and 3-month SNAP-IV change.
evidence_signal: In 309 participants, ADHD PGS was associated with higher overall SNAP-IV scores and EA PGS with lower scores, while model estimates suggested up to 92% upper-bound classification accuracy when clinical and genetic features were combined.
watch_item: The machine learning models did not empirically generalize, so the results need external validation before clinical use.
paper_title: Polygenic and machine learning analysis of medication response in a prospective pediatric cohort initiating ADHD medication
